title.narrative: Rapid Response Window 2021 - Women Peace and Humanitarian Fund
Rapid Response Window 2021 - Women Peace and Humanitarian Fund

description.narrative: The RRW’s overall objective is to support women’s meaningful participation during all stages, at all tracks, and at all levels of peace processes. It is a funding mechanism which will support strategic civil society led short-term initiatives to influence and participate in formal, national or international processes. The scope for requests is purposely diverse and open to encompass demands to support women’s meaningful participation through punctual interventions which need urgent support. While the scope is large, initiatives will be short in duration aiming to address rapidly a specific gap with an identified impact-specific action at different stages: - Before the peace negotiations: preparation/design - During the negotiations: gender provisions/women’s inputs - After the negotiations: implementation and monitoring The RRW will serve as a demand-driven and context-specific multi-partner funding mechanism for rapid, flexible and short/medium term support to civil society organizations. Funding support under the RRW is open to all ODA countries, beyond the eligible countries under WPHF. The RRW is reflected in the overall WPHF as being part of Outcome 4: Increased representation and leadership of women in formal and informal peace processes and/or implementation of peace agreements. 4.1 Number and/or percentage of women that influence or participate in formal and informal peace processes or negotiations (by role [mediator/adviser/stakeholder]) 4.2 Existence of gender responsive provisions in peace agreements, dialogues, and/or decision-making processes 4.3 Types of strategies used/implemented to participate in and contribute to the peace process and/or implementation of a peace agreement The RRW project is to "enable the effective establishment and delivery of the Rapid Response Window’s Outcome result and indicators." The results frame work is found in Annex A of the Project document. There will be four underlying out-puts: Output 1.1. Quality technical and advisory support to the RRW and its decision-making structures is provided Output 1.2. Efficient, effective, and timely management of the Rapid Response Window and direct implementation of support is ensured Output 1.3. Efficient, effective and timely management of INGO partnerships is ensured Output 1.4. Communications, capacity building and Knowledge Management is provided to the Rapid Response Window The out-puts are underpinned with Indicators and targets, Means of verification/Sources of Information and Activities in a results frame work.

The Women Peace and Humanitaran Fund has approached Sida for funding to set-up, start and carry out the global project "Rapid Response Window" during 2021 via a Multi Donor Trust Fund modality.
The Rapid Response Window´s overall objective is to support women’s meaningful participation during all stages, at all tracks, and at all levels of peace processes. It is a funding mechanism which will support strategic civil society led short-term initiatives to influence and participate in formal, national or international processes. The scope for requests is purposely diverse and open to encompass demands to support women’s meaningful participation through punctual interventions which need urgent support. The Rapid Response Window will implement the intervention together with five global international NGOs.
The full budget amounts to USD 5 600 280 (ca 47 MSEK) and the present funding gap is approximately 3 MUSD (ca 25 MSEK). Germany, Canada and Nowraw are among the donors which have already contributed to the fund.

Women Peace and Humanitaran Fund har kontaktat Sida för att söka finansiering för att starta och genomföra det globala projektet "Rapid Response Window" under 2021 via en Multi Donor Trust Fund.
Det övergripande målet för Rapid Response Windows är att stödja kvinnors meningsfulla deltagande under alla delar, i alla spår och på alla nivåer av fredsprocesser. Det är en finansieringsmekanism som kommer att stödja strategiska civilsamhällesledda kortsiktiga initiativ för att påverka och delta i informella, formella, nationella eller internationella fredsprocesser. Utrymmet för ansökningar är avsiktligt öppet för att kunna omfatta behov att kunna stödja kvinnors meningsfulla deltagande genom punktinsatser för akut stöd. Rapid Response Window kommer att genomföras tillsammans med fem globala internationella icke-statliga organisationer.
Hela budgeten uppgår till 5 600 280 USD (cirka 47 MSEK) och det nuvarande finansieringsgapet är cirka 3 MUSD (cirka 25 MSEK). Exemplevis Tyskland, Kanada och Norge har redan bidragit till fonden.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
In a nutshell, the RRW reports it has "supported 20 civil society initiatives by 45 organizations in 15 countries, involving 290 women peacebuilders and activists participating in formal peace processes, negotiations or peace agreement implementation, and directly benefiting over 26 000 people (72 per cent women)". Most of the supported interventions focused on Track 2 peace processes (47 procent) and the implementation of peace agreements (41 procent).
Key achievements and results have been focused on peace negotiations or implementation of peace accords in for example DRC, Libya, Yemen, Cameroon, Syria, Ethiopia and Eswatini. It is evident from this years report (compared to the first year) that the RRW is now using all its tools to support women peace builders and their increased participation in Track 1 & 2 processes and that more data is therefore available to showcase the role of RRW.
Track 1
- DRC: Seven women from Africa Women Leadership Network and Focus Droit et Accès participated in the third round of consultations on the recommendations for effective measures on the Disarmament, Demobilization and Community Rehabilitation Program in November 2022 as part of the Nairobi Peace Talks process. - Libya: Five women leaders were at the table of negotiations in Libya in August 2022 during the dialogue between Libyan armed groups in Norway with the participation of the European Union. - Yemen: Six women - including women living with disabilities - from AMENA Foundation were engaged in a workshop with the office of the UN Special Envoy on how to engage with decision makers and effective approaches to influence peace process in the country. - Cameroon: Five indigenous women in Cameroon from Reach Out Cameroon (ROC) participated in the Ndian Peace Conference led by the Prime Minister and traditional leaders in April 2022.
Track 2
As mentioned above, most of the RRW initiatives have been on Track 2 processes and the implementation of peace agreements. This has resulted in womens rights organizations having developed concrete recommendations and key actions to influence peace processes and include womens voices. WPHF reports that this had led to innovative strategies to raise awareness and inform stakeholders; and to enhance gender provisions of peace agreements and their implementation. Furthermore, key actors have been able to mobilize concrete and efficient solutions to improve womens influence in a sustainable way, especially through the establishment of monitoring mechanisms in different parts of the world. Examples below:
- Syria: Badael engaged 16 women activists in Syria - including key national actors, civil society leaders, international stakeholders and media representatives - to establish linkages and facilitate coalition building and knowledge exchange between peace process advisors to identify mechanisms, institutions and opportunities available for women inside Syria to participate in the peace process. As a result, over 170 women peace builders presented recommendations to members and co-chairs of the Constitutional Committee for the Syrian Negotiation Board and The Syrian National Coalition for Revolutionary and Opposition Forces. - Ethiopia: 70 women activists engaged by the Ethiopian Womens Coalition (EWC) established a network and community of women peace builders for womens inclusion in National Dialogue processes. - Eswatini: Two women representatives in Eswatini from Women Unlimited Eswatini (WUE) participated in the Regional Women Peace and Security workshop led by the Southern African Development Countries, SADC, ensuring Eswatini womens experiences are shared and resolved at decision-making tables. - Cameroon: 40 women peacebuilders from Reach out Cameroon (ROC) were also engaged in the National Dialogue mechanisms to ensure gender-sensitive monitoring was carried out of the implementation of the Dialogue.
The RRW is managed in partnership with seven INGOs whereof three are Sida partners (Sustainable Peace Strategy): Conciliation Resources, Global Partnership for the Prevention of Armed Conflict (GPPAC) and the Womens International League for Peace and Freedom (WILPF). One is a former partner to the strategy: Inclusive Peace and one gets support form MOFA: International Civil Society Action Network (ICAN). The other two are also well know to Sida: Cordaid and Netherlands Institute for Multiparty Democracy (NIMD). The latter has over time had various cooperations with Sida. These partners support the implementation of selected RRW projects, in the management of grants, and provide technical and strategic support to CSOs, for example in Mozambique and Palestine.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
